title: Tidal bans AI-generated music
lede: Variety reports that Tidal will remove every wholly AI-generated track from December 9, about five months after it started demonetizing AI songs.

points: Robert Andersen, Tidal lead at parent company Block, says 43% of tracks delivered in the last 90 days were detected as AI-generated.
He says 96% of AI songs get zero plays; the ban removes 29 million tracks and rejects 80,000 to 85,000 a day.
The earlier policy required AI-generated or AI-assisted labels and banned tracks that impersonate established artists.
Apple Music plans labels, while Spotify tags AI artists as an AI Persona and has pulled tens of millions of spam tracks.

points.text: The top thread expects AI to seep into synths and effects until the line between AI music and ordinary tools blurs and a ban stops making sense.
Listeners split: one who mostly plays AI jazz wanted a filter rather than a ban, and a reply says many will pay to keep it out.
Commenters trade tells for spotting Suno output, from the same few voices to near-identical lyric cadence.
Others ask where AI-assisted begins, pointing to vocal synths and rendering tools where the musician still writes every note.
